_comment: Where tools/title_progress.py finds Crackdown and what cannot be read from its sources: the groups its system binding switches on, where the graphics binding lives, known problems and title-specific work. Paths are this machine's checkouts; nothing of the title is in this repository.
name: Crackdown

sys.where: all eight groups, opt-in on `main`: `--any360_sys_groups=stateless,files,objects,threads,memory,xam,input,audio`; no call reaches ReXGlue's kernel then

gfx.where: opt-in on `main`: `--any360_gpu=true` (resolution scale, host MSAA, pipeline cache); 160-220 FPS at 1440p with 4x MSAA in the city on an RTX 5070 Ti
todo: `main` needs an Any360 checkout next to the repository to build (`CRACKDOWN_ANY360_DIR`, by default `../any360`): make it optional, as in The Simpsons Game, or fetched by the build.

The game-side draw records (HLE renderer, milestones H1-H4 below) feed a renderer that knows the game's passes instead of translating Xenos commands; they move onto `any360::gfx` once the emulated path is the fallback only.

next: Native renderer from the game's own draw records: H2 switch the scene one render pass at a time (depth prepass first), H3 every pass native, H4 draws recorded on several threads and per-object motion vectors.
FSR upscaling on the Steam Deck, which needs those motion vectors.
Steam Deck as the primary target: the same Vulkan renderer on Linux, CPU-bound today.
Follow upstream releases (merged up to v0.6.2).
open: Single-tile scene (experimental): a shadow ghost is left at some spots.
Keyboard and mouse through `any360::sys` input are not checked (gamepad and vibration are).
